change: Recover stopped deferred-discovery jobs from their original permission, exact execution anchor and unique native history. Persist Claude's independently observed Herdr idle and transcript boundary before the completion transaction, and revalidate that evidence on cold recovery.
behavior: Deferred recovery validates old process lifetime, project/workspace/root, dispatch identity, execution UUID and native header, then scans bounded history candidates without sending input.
The active execution's unique native history supersedes an older cache. Ambiguous, missing, foreign and out-of-scope histories cannot authorize replacement agents or fabricated fresh sessions.
Claude assistant text is a candidate. Native observation must also confirm the mounted identity and idle state against the anchored transcript; only the authority commits the resulting receipt.

Claude recovery checks receipt/job/execution/session/process binding, file identity and recorded boundary digest, then rereads current history. Hook continuation, changed replies, replaced/rewritten history or foreign receipts cannot report old success.
Ordinary Claude observation validation failures quarantine the affected provider rather than shutting down the entire actor.
Stopped readers drain bounded observation chunks up to 64 MiB; incomplete trailing records remain uncertain instead of releasing a premature result.

New retry attempts discard prior native execution, scope, cancellation, termination, dispatch and terminal-observation fields, and acquire a new execution and send permission. Other provider options retain their previous semantics.
